Slots.maps_to: `Encounter.slots` (monsters/base.py) -- the sim's `DENSE_VEGETATION_EVENT_ENCOUNTER` (`_WrigglerNestEncounter`, dense_vegetation.py:16-30) passes no `slots=` argument, so it defaults to `()`, where DenseVegetationEventEncounter.cs:13 declares `["wriggler1","wriggler2","wriggler3","wriggler4"]`. Executed: `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e9.py slots-not-ported` prints `()` for the sim side.
Slots.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). The `Encounter` dataclass already had `slots`/`monster_slots` and `CreatureCmd.add(slot_name=)` re-sorts on them (shipped round 7 for Fabricator/Ovicopter); this unit simply never declared its row. It does now, transcribed from the C# `Slots` override and `GenerateMonsters`' `(model, slot)` pairs, and `CombatState.__init__` routes every roster through `Encounter.seat_in_slots` so the seventeen `create_monsters` overrides are seated too. Regression tests: test/test_encounter_slots.py.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: encounter/_slots_not_ported: the named slot row is not represented on the sim's Encounter instance at all. Traced to its one consequence, `CombatState.sort_enemies_by_slot_name` (combat.py) -- it no-ops whenever `encounter.slots` is empty, and the same probe confirms it is never invoked for the INITIAL roster construction in the first place (only `CreatureCmd.add`'s mid-combat spawn path calls it), so an empty `slots` costs nothing for this unit today: the 4 Wrigglers are never re-seated after construction because nothing summons into this encounter's row. See the `GenerateMonsters` entry below for the paired half of this same finding (the returned monsters' slot names).

HasScene.maps_to: no sim counterpart -- the sim has no scene/rendering system whatsoever (`grep -rn HasScene\|CreateScene\|GetAssetPaths sts2_rl/` finds nothing anywhere in the tree). `HasScene` (DenseVegetationEventEncounter.cs:15, true) only gates whether `EncounterModel.GetAssetPaths` (EncounterModel.cs:328-343) preloads a Godot scene file -- a pure asset-loading concern with no effect on RNG draws, monster composition, or any other observable game-state.
HasScene.rationale: Unreachable: the headless sim has no renderer, no scene graph and no asset-preload pipeline of any kind to receive this flag.

AllPossibleMonsters.maps_to: no explicit sim field (same absence as every other unit in this batch, see battleworn_dummy_event's entry for the whole-tree grep); `DENSE_VEGETATION_EVENT_ENCOUNTER.monster_classes` is `[Wriggler]*4`, which already equals the C# superset `{Wriggler}` (DenseVegetationEventEncounter.cs:17) exactly, since GenerateMonsters never branches on anything.
AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: The concept has no sim representation, but for a fixed, non-branching roster the composition IS the superset, so nothing is lost for this unit specifically.

GenerateMonsters.maps_to: `_WrigglerNestEncounter.create_monsters` (dense_vegetation.py:20-24) overrides the base `Encounter.create_monsters`. Roster: 4 Wrigglers, matching the C# `foreach (string slot in Slots)` loop (DenseVegetationEventEncounter.cs:22-27) count for count. Order: the sim builds `for slot in range(1, 5)`, i.e. wriggler1..4 in order, matching the C# loop's `Slots` iteration order element for element. Draw count: BOTH sides draw zero from any Rng inside this method (no `base.Rng` call anywhere in the C# body; the sim's loop only calls the `Wriggler` constructor, which draws HP off the passed-in Niche/legacy stream, a separate concern -- not this method's own draw). Move-selection parity: C#'s `Wriggler.GenerateMoveStateMachine` picks the opening move via `Creature.SlotName == "wriggler1"/"wriggler3"` (odd->NASTY_BITE) vs `"wriggler2"/"wriggler4"` (even->WRIGGLE); the sim's `Wriggler.__init__` (monsters/overgrowth/phrog_parasite.py:22-35) takes a `slot: int` constructor argument instead and computes the identical odd/even split directly (`slot % 2 == 1`), fed the same 1..4 sequence -- so the OUTCOME matches turn for turn even though the mechanism differs. Slot pairing (the (Monster, slot) half of the C# return value): NOT reproduced -- `create_monsters` never sets `.slot_name` on any of the 4 Wrigglers (confirmed: `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e9.py slots-not-ported` prints `[None, None, None, None]`), where C# returns `(wriggler, "wriggler1")` etc. This is the same root cause as, and the paired half of, the `Slots` entry above.

It does now, transcribed from the C# `Slots` override and `GenerateMonsters`' `(model, slot)` pairs, and `CombatState.__init__` routes every roster through `Encounter.seat_in_slots` so the seventeen `create_monsters` overrides are seated too. Regression tests: test/test_encounter_slots.py.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: encounter/_slots_not_ported (same mechanism as the `Slots` hook above): the returned monsters carry no slot identity, only roster/order/move-selection are reproduced. Dormant for the reason given on `Slots`: nothing re-sorts or re-seats this encounter's enemies after construction, and the odd/even move split -- the one thing that would actually need slot identity -- is independently recovered via the constructor's positional `slot:int` argument.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.maps_to: EncounterModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false (EncounterModel.cs:39, inherited, not re-overridden here). The sim never registers an Encounter as a hook listener anywhere (see battleworn_dummy_event's entry for the full call-site check).

guards.what: encounter/_entry_slug_mismatch: `DENSE_VEGETATION_EVENT_ENCOUNTER.entry` = `DENSE_VEGETATION_EVENT` (from `id="dense_vegetation_event"`), but the game's real `Id.Entry` for `DenseVegetationEventEncounter` is `DENSE_VEGETATION_EVENT_ENCOUNTER` (`StringHelper.Slugify(type.Name)`, confirmed via `ModelDb.GetEntry`) -- the sim's id drops the '_ENCOUNTER' suffix the class name actually carries. Executed: `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e9.py entry-slug-mismatch` prints MISMATCH.
guards.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). `Encounter` gained an explicit `entry_slug` field and `Encounter.entry` returns it when set, so this unit seeds `make_encounter_rng` with the game's real `ModelId.Entry` while keeping its sim id. A mechanical sweep of ALL 87 sim encounters against `src/Core/Models/Encounters/*.cs` (audit/tools/encounter_entry_sweep.py) found two more the unit batches had not checked — `fuzzy_wurm_crawler` (FuzzyWurmCrawlerWeak) and `overgrowth_crawlers_normal` (OvergrowthCrawlers) — and now reports MATCH for every one. Pinned by test/test_encounter_entry_slugs.py.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: Same mechanism as `battleworn_dummy_event/G1` and (LIVE) `punch_off_event/G1`. Dormant here because DenseVegetationEventEncounter.GenerateMonsters draws zero values from `base.Rng` (see the GenerateMonsters entry above), and `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e9.py dormant-4-zero-draws` confirms the sim's `create_monsters` output is byte-identical under two unrelated seeds -- so the wrong per-encounter Rng seed this unit builds in parity mode is never actually drawn from.
